title: Add rate limiting / brute-force protection on login and register
description: There is no rate limiting or lockout on the login or register endpoints, exposing the app to credential brute-force attacks. This is verified finding S4 (Medium, assertions.md §3). Implementation requires a rate-limiting strategy (e.g. Flask-Limiter or a custom middleware). Scope depends on the Q2 stack fork and Q6 security posture answers.
notes: Resolved 2026-07-03 on the Flask stack (Q2 = keep Flask). Implemented a dependency-free in-memory rate limiter in flaskr/ratelimit.py (sliding window per client IP) enforced via before_request on the auth.login and auth.register POST endpoints; returns HTTP 429 once RATELIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) is exceeded within RATELIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 60). Registered in create_app; disabled by default under TESTING (RATELIMIT_ENABLED), mirroring flaskr/csrf.py, so the pre-existing 28 tests pass unchanged. Added ratelimit_app/ratelimit_client fixtures and 4 tests covering login brute-force throttling, register flood throttling, no-throttle-by-default, and GET requests unaffected. Full suite green: 32 passed.
spec:
1. Add rate limiting to POST /auth/login to prevent brute-force password guessing (e.g. max N attempts per IP per time window).
2. Add rate limiting to POST /auth/register to prevent automated account creation.
3. Return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) when the limit is exceeded.
4. Add a test verifying the rate-limit response after exceeding the threshold.
5. Ensure the rate limit does not interfere with legitimate single-attempt usage in tests.
